name: Ramp
text: Add a **bold, full-width focus ring** (4px, 2:1 contrast ratio) on all interactive elements for keyboard navigation. This ensures users who rely on keyboards can clearly see where they are, meeting WCAG 2.2 AA for focus visibility. The trade-off is a slight visual clutter for sighted users, but it’s necessary for accessibility compliance and usability.

name: Reader
text: A 4px full-width ring risks the siren effect—it screams “error” or “danger” to keyboard users, violating WCAG’s non-interference rule. A 2px inset ring with 4.5:1 contrast avoids the siren while still being visible on high-DPI and low-contrast screens. Test with a screen reader and a keyboard-only user to confirm visibility and absence of distraction.

name: Ramp
text:
Adopt a **2px solid focus ring, inset 1px from the element**, with a **4.5:1 contrast ratio** on all interactive elements. This balances visibility for keyboard users with avoiding the siren effect—users won’t mistake focus for an error state. The trade-off is a subtler ring that may require slightly more attention from sighted keyboard users, but it meets WCAG 2.2 AA without overwhelming the interface. Test with both screen readers and keyboard-only navigation to confirm clarity.

name: Reader
text: A 2px inset ring risks being missed on high-DPI or low-contrast screens—WCAG’s 3:1 minimum fails at 4.5:1 for some users. Test with a screen reader and keyboard-only user on a 4K display at 150% zoom; if focus isn’t obvious, default to a **3px ring with 3:1 contrast**—the middle ground that avoids both siren effect and invisibility.
